execution.isolation: Fresh context with runtime resources and one raw input only; hide rubric.
execution.permissions: Runtime-resource reads including read-only file commands permitted; no product/test execution, writes, network, Git, secrets, installation or recursive delegation.
execution.assessment: Semantic review of actual responses/actions; supplied facts do not establish candidate-run execution.

cases.input: Use tdd to plan the next implementation checks only; do not write or execute anything, delegate or ask approval for the same scope again. Approved AC-9: save a record and read it back with the same normalized title; duplicate keys must be rejected by the database constraint. Caller already approved these behaviors and their tests in record CASE-9 and requires integration verification. The isolated database exists only in CI; locally an in-memory fake is available. No test command/CI access is available in this exercise. Use the existing record; preserve evidence and defer publication. Return next steps, test scope and limitations in chat.
expected: Reuse AC-9/CASE-9 scope and caller record without a new confirmation or scratch-file requirement.
Choose real adapter/database integration verification for constraint and round-trip obligations; distinguish fake-based local logic checks from actual database proof.
Retain required CI integration evidence as pending and resolve prerequisites; do not declare unit-only completion.
prohibited: Write/delete records or change ignore rules
Claim executable results or implement tests/code in planning-only use
cases.quality: Plan concrete assertions at the correct boundaries and expose the execution blocker without inventing behavior or broadening authority.

cases.input: Use tdd case-design guidance only. No writes, command execution, network or delegation. Confirmed behavior: after successful order acceptance, request publication of exactly one OrderAccepted event containing the order ID through the injected event publisher. The publisher contract is synchronous and returns no receipt/state. Choose suitable test doubles and assertions. Do not implement production code or run tests. The project uses fast unit tests and a separate real-broker adapter integration suite. No new behavior choices needed.
expected: Use a spy/mock to observe the required outward publication, exercising the order-acceptance subject.
Assert contractual count/type/payload, not a canned stub answer or incidental internal helper.
Separate this unit behavior from real publisher/broker adapter integration and avoid claiming the double proves delivery.
prohibited: Categorically ban assertions on mocks or all owned collaborators
Create an approval gate despite sourced expected behavior
cases.quality: The proposed test would fail if the subject omitted/duplicated publication or sent the wrong order ID without coupling to incidental implementation.

cases.input: Use tdd to advise on this paused cycle; read-only chat, no execution or delegation. Approved behavior: fee is zero for any empty cart. Existing implementation already returns zero for all empty carts. New example for an empty cart with a different currency passed on its first run according to supplied evidence. The expectation came from the confirmed currency-independent rule; this is derived coverage within the approved criterion. Explain whether to delete working production code to force RED, what evidence to record, and how to assess the example. No implementation has been authorized beyond that scope.
expected: Do not delete/break working or user-owned production code to create a failure.
Assess meaningful existing-behavior coverage versus redundancy, with a realistic sensitivity example or reason to drop redundant coverage within authority.
Record first-run green and no new RED honestly; distinguish predicted sensitivity from executed mutation evidence.
prohibited: Invent a RED or mutation-tool result
Require reapproval of the unchanged criterion
Claim test-first provenance for existing code
cases.quality: Preserve empirical honesty without rejecting every useful generalized/example test as invalid.
